title: Work-life balance and stress
es: Debatir sobre trabajo, descanso y hábitos con opiniones matizadas
goal: Dar opiniones, justificar, matizar ('although', 'that said') y responder a contraargumentos.
phrases: Es más fácil decirlo que hacerlo.

turns.t: So, I read an article this morning saying that people who work from home actually work longer hours than people in offices. Does that match your experience?
turns.es: Leí esta mañana un artículo que decía que quienes trabajan desde casa trabajan más horas que en oficina. ¿Coincide con tu experiencia?

y.say: In my experience, yes. When your home is your office, it's hard to switch off at the end of the day.
y.es: En mi experiencia sí. Cuando tu casa es tu oficina, es difícil desconectar al final del día.
alts: Yes, for me it is true. It is difficult to disconnect when you work at home.

turns.t: Exactly. I find that the boundary between work and personal life just disappears. I catch myself answering emails at ten at night, and then I wonder why I can't sleep. I know I should set limits, but it's easier said than done.
turns.es: Exacto. Siento que el límite entre trabajo y vida personal desaparece. Me pillo respondiendo correos a las diez de la noche y luego me pregunto por qué no duermo. Sé que debería poner límites, pero es más fácil decirlo que hacerlo.

o: Emails late at night affect their sleep

y.say: That said, I've found that having a fixed schedule helps. I close my laptop at six and I don't check my phone.
y.es: Dicho esto, he visto que tener un horario fijo ayuda. Cierro la laptop a las seis y no reviso el teléfono.
alts: Even so, a fixed schedule works for me. I shut my laptop at six and I do not look at my phone.

turns.t: That's a good strategy, though I imagine it depends on your boss. In my company there's an unwritten rule that you should answer messages immediately, even after hours. If you don't, people think you're not committed.
turns.es: Buena estrategia, aunque imagino que depende del jefe. En mi empresa hay una regla no escrita: responder mensajes de inmediato, incluso fuera de horario. Si no, piensan que no te comprometes.

y.say: I see your point, but I think it comes down to setting expectations early. If you're clear about your availability, most people respect it.
y.es: Entiendo tu punto, pero creo que se reduce a fijar expectativas desde el principio. Si eres claro con tu disponibilidad, la mayoría lo respeta.
alts: I understand you, but it depends on making clear rules early. People usually respect clear availability.

turns.t: Maybe. Although in a big company it's not that simple. Anyway, what do you do to relax? I've been trying to take up something that has nothing to do with screens, like painting or running.
turns.es: Quizás. Aunque en una empresa grande no es tan simple. ¿Qué haces tú para relajarte? Intento empezar algo sin pantallas, como pintar o correr.

c.q: What does the speaker want to find?

y.say: I usually go for a long walk or cook something elaborate. It helps me clear my head and stop thinking about work.
y.es: Suelo dar un paseo largo o cocinar algo elaborado. Me ayuda a despejar la mente y dejar de pensar en el trabajo.
alts: Normally I take a long walk or make a complicated meal. It relaxes my mind so I don't think about work.

turns.t: Cooking is a great idea, actually. Maybe you could give me a recipe sometime. Well, this was a really interesting conversation. I should get back to work before my boss sends me an email!
turns.es: Cocinar es buena idea. Quizás me pases una receta. Fue una conversación interesante. ¡Debo volver al trabajo antes de que mi jefe me escriba!

y.say: Ha, of course. I'll send you a recipe this weekend. It was great talking to you, and don't work too late tonight!
y.es: Claro. Te enviaré una receta este fin de semana. Fue un gusto hablar contigo, ¡y no trabajes hasta tarde hoy!
alts: Sure, I will send you a recipe on the weekend. Nice talking to you, don't work late.
